clue.text: Joined the Left in ideal arrangement

indicators.note: an arrangement of the word ideal, with the added letter, puts its letters into a new order

explanation.surface: A political alliance in which the Left signs up to some idealised scheme.
explanation.walkthrough: 'arrangement' signals the anagram of L plus IDEAL.
explanation.definitionFit: Allied nations are joined together in an alliance, so the two words are synonyms.

clue.text: The princess's baby with a following

indicators.note: the letter a comes after, or follows, the baby in this clue

explanation.surface: A royal princess's newborn has gathered a crowd of admirers.
explanation.walkthrough: The 's of 'princess's' is 'is', linking the definition to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: An infanta is the title of a daughter of a Spanish or Portuguese king, a princess.

clue.text: Jolly Roger gives the sack without need, heartless fool

indicators.note: without in its old sense of outside, so the sack goes round the other pieces

parts.note: to lack something is to need it

indicators.note: a heartless word loses its middle letters, leaving only the outer pair here

parts.note: a fool, the starting word before its middle is taken away

explanation.surface: Someone fired from their job finds it needless and calls the boss a heartless fool.
explanation.walkthrough: 'without' is used in its old sense of outside, and 'heartless' strips the middle of the fool.
explanation.definitionFit: The Jolly Roger is the pirate flag, traditionally a black banner bearing a skull and crossbones.

clue.text: Sweet play

explanation.definitionFit: A trifle is a layered British pudding of sponge, custard and cream; to trifle with something is to toy or play with it.

clue.text: Having a dog in view as guard

indicators.note: the dog sits inside the word for view, as the clue says it is in view

parts.note: a cur is a dog, usually a mongrel

explanation.surface: Keeping a dog in sight as a watchdog.
explanation.definitionFit: To guard something is to make it safe, and to secure it means the same.

clue.text: A serving man gets near-distraught

indicators.note: distraught means greatly upset, so these letters are thrown into disorder

explanation.surface: A waiter is almost at the end of his tether.
explanation.walkthrough: 'serving man' suggests a waiter or butler; it is a man serving in the army. 'distraught' signals the anagram of GETS NEAR.
explanation.definitionFit: A sergeant is a non-commissioned officer, a man serving in the army.

clue.text: A swimmer set about exercise and did well

indicators.note: set about here means placed around, so the fish surrounds the exercise

parts.note: a cod is a fish, a swimmer

explanation.surface: A swimmer took up a training routine and performed well.
explanation.definitionFit: To cope is to manage or get by successfully, so having coped is having done well enough.

clue.text: Repeatedly rigid-it's cramp

parts.note: the prefix re- means again, or repeatedly

explanation.surface: A complaint that rigid rules keep cramping one's style.
explanation.definitionFit: To cramp is to hamper or confine, and to restrict means to limit in the same way.

clue.text: Giving pounds and pounds or a large figure for a letter

parts.note: L is the abbreviation for pounds sterling, from Latin libra
D is the Roman numeral for 500, a large figure

explanation.surface: A rich benefactor hands out pound after pound, or a big sum, for each letter written.
explanation.walkthrough: 'a letter' is someone who lets property, not a written message.
explanation.definitionFit: A landlord rents out property, so he is one who lets: a letter.

clue.text: Intend writing about one of the great rivers of Europe

indicators.note: about here means around, so the writing goes round the river

parts.words: one of the great rivers of Europe
parts.note: the Po is Italy's longest river

explanation.surface: Someone means to write an essay about a major European river.
explanation.definitionFit: To propose doing something is to intend or plan it.

clue.text: The man's in debt after using his Visa account

indicators.note: using here means the answer draws its letters from within the words that follow

explanation.surface: A man has run up debts after spending on his Visa card.
explanation.walkthrough: The letters run across 'visA ACcount'; Isaac stands for a man in general.
explanation.definitionFit: Isaac is a man's name, the biblical son of Abraham.

clue.text: The novel "Green Lady-fictitious, ofcourse

indicators.note: novel means new, so the two named words take a new form

explanation.surface: A novel titled Green Lady is, naturally, a work of fiction.
explanation.walkthrough: 'novel' looks like a book; it is the anagram signal for GREEN LADY.
explanation.definitionFit: Something of legend is mythical or invented, so legendary can mean fictitious.

clue.text: Fish key is presented to the Spanish

explanation.surface: A key handed over to Spanish people for a fish.
explanation.definitionFit: An eel is a long snakelike fish.

clue.text: No work, no tax to pay!

explanation.definitionFit: Duty can mean work or obligation, so free of it is no work; duty is also a tax on imports, so duty-free goods carry none.

clue.text: A virtuous probationer?

parts.note: a virtuous person has ..., and split that way the phrase is also a beginner on trial in a religious order

explanation.definitionFit: A novice is a probationary member of a religious order, and a newcomer generally.

clue.text: After a shoot-out use would be made of a dryer

indicators.note: out means unsettled or disordered, so the letters around it are rearranged

explanation.surface: After a gunfight the place would be put to use as a dryer.
explanation.walkthrough: 'out' (from 'shoot-out') signals the anagram of A SHOOT USE.
explanation.definitionFit: An oast house is a building with a kiln for drying hops, a dryer.

clue.text: Titled people-one is in hospital in London

indicators.note: is in tells us the word one sits inside the hospital's name

parts.note: Bart's is St Bartholomew's, a famous London hospital

explanation.surface: Aristocrats include one who is in a London hospital.
explanation.walkthrough: St Bartholomew's, known as Bart's, is a famous hospital in the City of London.
explanation.definitionFit: Baronets hold a hereditary title, the rank just below a baron.

clue.text: Skilful at aquiring a little money

indicators.note: acquiring (as printed) means taking in, so the small coin goes inside the word at

parts.note: p is a penny, a small amount of money

explanation.surface: Being good at making a bit of money.
explanation.definitionFit: Apt can mean quick to learn or skilled, as in an apt pupil.

clue.text: Dolt raising a weapon that might well gain him entry

definitions.text: that might well gain him entry

indicators.note: in a down clue raising means lifting a word so it reads from bottom to top

parts.note: a sap is a dolt or fool

explanation.surface: A fool brandishes a weapon hoping it will get him in.
explanation.walkthrough: In a down clue 'raising' turns the fool upwards.
explanation.definitionFit: A secret word spoken to a guard admits the speaker, so it gains him entry.

clue.text: A Greek character had a meal on returning

indicators.note: returning means going back, so the meal word is read in the reverse direction

explanation.surface: A Greek man ate on getting home.
explanation.definitionFit: Eta is the seventh letter of the Greek alphabet.

clue.text: There's many a criminal with a 27 in Spain

parts.note: M, a thousand in Roman numerals, stands for many
an old lag is a convict, a criminal

explanation.surface: Lots of crooks are hiding out in a Spanish resort.
explanation.walkthrough: LAG is British slang for a convict. 27 refers to the answer at 27-down.
explanation.definitionFit: Malaga is a city and port on Spain's Costa del Sol, a location in Spain.

clue.text: Some women beam at the steward offering a rug

indicators.note: some here means a part of the following words, so the letters are taken from within them

explanation.surface: Several women smile at the steward who is handing out a blanket.
explanation.definitionFit: A mat is a small floor covering, a rug.

clue.text: Flighty creature getting a flat in disorder

indicators.note: disorder means a muddle, so the preceding letters are jumbled

explanation.surface: A scatterbrained person finds their flat in a mess.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Flighty' suggests a giddy person; it means able to fly. 'disorder' signals the anagram of A FLAT IN.
explanation.definitionFit: A fantail is a pigeon with a fan-shaped tail, a creature of flight.

clue.text: Cut down, which is hard to understand

explanation.definitionFit: To abstract a text is to summarise or shorten it; abstract ideas are theoretical and difficult to grasp.

clue.text: Article written in bed before the French official

indicators.note: written in means put into, so the article goes inside the word bed

explanation.surface: An article written in bed before a French officer.
explanation.definitionFit: A beadle is a minor parish or church officer.

clue.text: Sort of shirt (coarse) seen in a depressed area

explanation.surface: A rough kind of shirt worn in a poor district.
explanation.definitionFit: A trough is a long low hollow, a depression in the ground or in weather charts.

clue.text: Mixed with the company representative round 27

parts.note: an MP is a Member of Parliament, an elected representative
27 refers to 27-down's answer, a location, which here means site

explanation.surface: Mixing with the company rep somewhere around.
explanation.walkthrough: 27 refers to 27-down, whose answer here gives SITE.
explanation.definitionFit: A composite thing is made of several parts, mixed together.

annotationWithheld.clue: Where the speed should be about

clue.text: Away from home, cook may appear overcome

parts.note: to do food is to cook it

explanation.surface: Away from home, the cook seems overwhelmed.
explanation.definitionFit: To outdo someone is to beat or surpass them.

clue.text: No tears affected the American politician

indicators.note: affected means altered, so the letters are changed in order

explanation.surface: The US politician was unmoved and shed no tears.
explanation.walkthrough: 'affected' signals the anagram of NO TEARS.
explanation.definitionFit: A senator is a member of the US Senate, an American politician.

clue.text: Attempt toretain the remains of a momentary illumination

indicators.note: to retain, printed as one word, means to hold within, so the attempt goes round the remains

parts.note: a fling is a try or attempt
ash is what remains after burning

explanation.surface: Trying to keep the remains of a brief flash of light.
explanation.walkthrough: 'toretain' is 'to retain' run together in print.
explanation.definitionFit: A brief flash of light lasts only a moment.

clue.text: Rise as about to close

explanation.surface: Getting up as the day nears its end.
explanation.definitionFit: To rise is to go up, and to ascend means the same.
